chunks: And in Nawādir al-Ḥikmah, it is narrated that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said:

Regarding a man whose wife caused ifḍāʾ to his bondwoman with her hand, he ruled that she should be appraised at one value while sound and at another value while afflicted with ifḍāʾ, then he would make her liable for the difference between soundness and defect, and he compelled her to keep her because she was no longer suitable for men.

key_terms.أَفْضَتِ: caused ifḍāʾ, a severe genital injury
key_terms.الصِّحَّةِ وَالْعَيْبِ: the state of soundness and the state of defect
key_terms.تُقَوَّمَ: to be appraised or assessed in value

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman causes ifḍāʾ injury to a bondwoman?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bodily injury inflicted by a wife upon her husband's bondwoman, specifically ifḍāʾ. It establishes financial liability based on the difference in market value before and after the injury, and it also rules that the injuring party must retain the bondwoman because the injury rendered her unsuitable for men.
